5716.colorWord: orange tower, yellow arms, black head and base

shape.description: Upright orange faceted tower about 8 slots tall on a black battery base with four short legs. Two floor cells long: back cell holds the tower, front cell holds an orange bowl tray whose rim is high at the front and whose floor slopes back to the tower foot. A black head caps the tower and reaches forward over the arms, with a curved groove on top. Three yellow arms, each with a C-shaped scoop at both ends, turn on horizontal axles sticking out of the tower front at three heights, one arm length apart, so a scoop at the top of one arm's turn meets a scoop at the bottom of the next; neighbouring arms turn opposite ways (IMG_0954, IMG_0955). A black dome sits at the tower foot behind the tray. On/off slide switch on the base front. M-63 sign plugs into the head back.
shape.sizeBasis: Rough estimate: one cell about 52 mm and one slot about 36 mm, scaled from Joey's hand in IMG_0954 and IMG_0956; no ruler measurement. Width includes arms and tray horns. Slot height cross-check: on trex_plans_02 outlet to foot divided by inlet to foot is 8 to 2, matching the h8 and h2 stacks.

accepts: a marble rolling off a block at the tray front (inferred, Level 2 E2)
two floor cells in a line

physics.batteries: 3 AAA in the base, screw cover on the back; slide Off/On switch
physics.behaviour: Marbles travel UP, never down. The motor turns the three scoop arms like wheels. The lowest arm's scoop dips into the tray at the foot and scoops up a marble, half a turn carries it to the top, where it rolls into the next arm's scoop coming round at the bottom; the top arm tips it into the head groove, and it leaves at the top on the left side as you face the tower. Adds about 6 slots of height. Carries plain and metal marbles alike. Start piece: the tray takes marbles by hand. Also works mid-line as a lift: in Levels 1 and 2 the T-Rex feeds it.

evidence.shows: The piece is named Elevator; 3 AAA batteries, cover on back

Inward red arrows at the foot from both sides on T-06 tracks, plain and metal marbles both at the foot; red curved arrow from head to a T-06 at the top left, ghost marble leaving; plain marble in lowest arm, metal in top arm
Real tower: head reaches over arms, three axled arms in alternating tilt, tray, dome, base switch with power symbol
Level 1: stands on B1-B2 facing E. T-02 from top of B3 (h2) wraps round the tray into the S side of the tower cell. Upstream is T-05 from B4 under the Rex tail, so the Rex feeds the foot
Level 1: T-04 joins the S side of the head to the D3 stack top (h8): the outlet
Level 2: stands on C2-D2 facing S. T-02 from A2 (h2) enters W side of foot; second T-02 joins W side of head to A2 top (h8)
Level 3: stands on K8-K9 facing W. T-02 from K7 enters S side of foot (viewer's right, the other inlet); T-04 joins N side of head to I7 top: outlet on viewer's left again
Level 2: E2 stack stands directly in front of the tray, C3 stack directly right of the tower cell
It scoops up a ball from the bottom and spins it up to the top

assumptions: Role start is inferred from Joey saying the app begins with a starting piece and his photographing this piece; he did not say the words. In Levels 1 and 2 the first piece upstream is M-28, and this tower is mid-line there.
Arms are driven by the base motor: no document states the drive, but the batteries, the name Elevator and the moving arms point there.
Tray port height and the Level 2 tray feed from E2 are inferred from the map and from no other route for the tail marble.
Height 8 for the outlet comes from all three levels joining it to a stack of height 8 (D3, A2, I7).
faces uses E=+x, W=-x, S=+y, N=-y, in the piece's own frame. Heights are slots above the floor when the piece stands on the floor or, where stated, above the top of its supports.

Arms turn all the way round (Joey: spins it up), each one arm length above the last so the scoops meet; the turning direction alternates, read from neighbouring arms leaning opposite ways in IMG_0955.
